title.narrative: Kenya Water Security and Climate Resilience Project

description.narrative: (a) increase access to irrigation water for project beneficiaries and (b) enhance the institutional framework and strengthen capacity for water security and climate resilience in certain areas of the territory of the Recipient.

The development objectives of the Water Security and Climate Resilience Project for Kenya are to (i) increase availability and productivity of irrigation water for project beneficiaries; and (ii) enhance the institutional framework and strengthen capacity for water security and climate resilience for the country. The project has three components. The first component is water resources development. This component will support climate resilience and water security for economic growth by financing water investments and by progressively building a longer-term investment pipeline. This component has following two sub-components: water sector investments; and water investment pipeline. The second component is effective water sector institutions. It will support the current sector institutions, as well as the preparation, implementation and full functioning of the new; legal and institutional framework resulting from alignments with the Constitution of Kenya 2010. It will also support integrated and participatory basin planning, including developing the requisite knowledge base and building capacity and institutional partnerships for effective water management and planning. The overall objective of this component will be to strengthen the enabling institutional and legal framework to sustainably advance Kenya's vast water sector investment program in order to achieve water security and climate resilience. It has following two sub-components: (i) support for water sector transition and reforms and (ii) strengthening water management and planning. The third component is support for project implementation. This component will support the establishment of the Project Management Unit (PMU) to provide for effective project implementation through the completion of the First Kenya Water Security and Climate Resilience Project (KWSCRP-1) and throughout the reform period. This component will finance the required office space, goods (e.g., vehicles), equipment (e.g., computers), staff, consultant services, travel, training and operating costs that will allow the PMU to carry out its responsibilities for project implementation.

title.narrative: Area provided with irrigation and drainage services (ha)

comment.narrative: Despite the project's success in increasing the irrigated area from 0.00 to the current 1,777 hectares, the end target will not be achieved by May 31st, when IDA funding concludes. By the end of the IDA funding period, it was projected that the irrigated area would reach 2,632 hectares (67%), with water delivered to blocks and TC3 amounting to 1,947 hectares (50%) and out growers receiving water for 685 hectares (18%). The Government will provide funding for the remaining works after the project's closure in May. Computation: The 534 hectares pertain to the Bunyala irrigation scheme land (block 8) that has been rehabilitated by the project, in addition to the out growers' area. The construction of tertiary canals in blocks 1-4 is completed, except for a 200-meter section of TC 4.5. Construction of tertiary canals in block 5 is ongoing. Our Results Framework defines access as water being either delivered to the farm/plot or available within 250 meters from the farm/plot.

title.narrative: Area provided with irrigation and drainage services (ha)

comment.narrative:
As of today, the total command area achieved for the tertiary canals completed in Blocks 1 through 9 is 1,216 hectares. This figure encompasses outgrowers within these blocks as well as those from other blocks, representing a 44% achievement of the target. It is important to note that 24 tertiary canals have been completed out of a planned total of 44 within these blocks, with progress hindered by the impact of rainfall on the earthworks. Upon completion of all 44 tertiary canals in Blocks 1 through 9, the total command area is projected to reach 2,855 hectares.
NOTE - end target value for this indicator is 3905ha. This is according to the last AF project paper.

title.narrative: Water Resources Authority (WRA) Established and Operational

comment.narrative: WRA has been fully established and is now operational. This includes its establishment under Section 11 of the Water Act 2016. The authority is fully staffed with qualified personnel and possesses the necessary planning and regulatory tools, including but not limited to a spatial knowledge base, decision-support systems, and a functional water resource monitoring network. Additionally, it has a functional management board constituted in accordance with the legal provisions of Kenya. The WRA also has an annual operational budget that is fully funded through a combination of sources, including government transfers.
